articles.title: A 'never-ending' cruise halted operations and told residents to disembark in Cambodia after fuel costs rose over 300%
articles.summary: Villa Vie's promise of a live-in, continuous voyage around the world has hit choppy waters after surging fuel prices squeezed its finances.
articles.body:
It was meant to be a never-ending residential cruise. Now, operations have halted.

Villa Vie Residences said it can no longer operate due to fuel expenses surging more than 300%.

Passengers Lanette Canen and John Bodi said they had "a deep sense of heartbreak" at having to leave their home.

A cruise ship selling the promise of a permanent life at sea has come to an abrupt stop.

Villa Vie Residences, which operates the residential cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey , announced on Tuesday that it had suspended operations in Cambodia amid steep increases in fuel costs.

The company said its monthly fuel expenses per cabin, which had previously averaged about $1,800, had risen as much as 344% in parts of Asia, to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000.

If you are or have been a resident of the Villa Vie Odyssey and have a story to share, get in touch with this reporter: jzitser@businessinsider.com.

The US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, and Iran's subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz — a vital chokepoint for global oil shipments — sent energy prices soaring around the world.

"Since the conflict began in late February, we have taken significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port," Villa Vie Residences said.

"Those measures have not been enough to offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs, and we have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses."

Lanette Canen and John Bodi, both 56, who have been residents of the Odyssey since it first set sail and run a YouTube channel called Living Life on a Cruise about their experiences onboard, said they were given only a few hours' notice to leave the ship.

"On October 27, 2026, we received notice from the CEO at around 6 a.m. that all residents had to disembark by 2 p.m. that day," the couple said. "We knew leaving was a possibility, but the eight-hour notice still surprised us."

The couple said their immediate reaction was "a deep sense of heartbreak" at needing to leave their home. "It was difficult to process the news while packing up our life and saying goodbye to the place we had come to love."

Villa Vie Residences sold permanent cabins on its 509-cabin ship, the Odyssey, ranging from $119,999 to $439,999. Its pitch to residents was a never-ending cruise around the world with stops at more than 400 ports of call and a global circumnavigation every three-and-a-half years.

The ship, which has a pool deck, spa, and a pickleball court, also offered five-year residencies, starting at $59,999.

articles.title: Boeing shares tumble after it releases cautious growth forecast
articles.summary: Boeing shares plunged Tuesday as the company's cautious production growth timeframe surprised Wall Street, deepening questions about how fast recent plane ce...
articles.body:
Boeing shares plunged Tuesday as the company's cautious production growth timeframe surprised Wall Street, deepening questions about how fast recent plane certification and defense procurement wins will translate to the bottom line.

The aviation giant ended the day down 10.7 percent, the worst performer in the Dow index, as investors reacted poorly to forecasts from Boeing leaders on a conference call.

Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg said the company does not expect 737 MAX output to reach 52 per month until the second half of 2027 as it must first "stabilize" output at 47 per month.

Raising 737 MAX output has been viewed by investors as central to revenue and profit growth. But Ortberg, who joined Boeing in the aftermath of safety disasters, defended the approach.

"We're making progress, but we still have more work to do, and I'm expecting it'll take us into next year to get fully stable at this rate," Ortberg said of the 47 planes per month, citing the need for greater predictability in wing production and with the production of fuselages at its Kansas operation.

"It's more important that we do this ramp right than what particular month we achieve a rate break," Ortberg said.

Ortberg also put a timeframe on when the company will achieve $10 billion in annual free cash flow, saying it will reach the key target of financial health in 2029.

After Ortberg gave this timeframe, shares fell further, suggesting analysts had expected a quicker pace.

"Everybody wants us to go faster. I get that, but we're going to stay disciplined as we ramp up here," Ortberg said.

Ortberg joined Boeing as CEO in August 2024 as the company struggled to move past a pair of deadly 737 MAX crashes and a near-catastrophic 737 MAX flight in January 2024 in which a window blew out mid-flight.

The company at the time faced criticism that the problems stemmed from a culture that chased quick payoffs while shortchanging safety.

Boeing is making "slow but steady" progress, aviation expert Richard Aboulafia of AeroDynamic Advisory said in an email to AFP. "But the supply chain remains a major concern and one that's only partly in Boeing's control."

Ortberg's comments came as Boeing reported a third-quarter loss of $116 million, compared with a loss of $5.3 billion in the year-ago period mostly from delays to certification of the 777X, the latest generation in Boeing's long-range, wide-body commercial jet family.

The results translated into a larger earnings-per-share loss than analysts expected, but shares did not move significantly after the earnings press release was published.

articles.title: Ibovespa opera em queda e já acumula perda de 14% na semana; dólar recua à espera do Fed | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana fechou com queda de 0,97%, a R$ 5,3502. Já a bolsa brasileira caiu 0,51%, aos 175.705 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana fechou com queda de 0,97%, a R$ 5,3502. Já a bolsa brasileira caiu 0,51%, aos 175.705 pontos.
articles.body:
O Ibovespa , principal índice acionário da bolsa brasileira, opera mais uma vez em queda nesta quarta-feira (28), com um recuo de 1,38% perto das 10h30, aos 173.413 pontos . Na semana, já acumula perdas de 14,56%. Já o dólar caía 0,40% no mesmo horário, cotado a R$ 5,3282 .

O principal destaque da sessão fica com a nova decisão de juros do Federal Reserve ( Fed , o banco central dos Estados Unidos ). No Brasil, investidores voltam as atenções para o quadro fiscal, após a reeleição do presidente Lula (PT) no último domingo e em meio a promessas do governo sobre o resultado primário e a reforma tributária. (entenda mais abaixo)

▶️ O foco do mercado estará com a nova decisão de juros do Fed, prevista para o meio da tarde. Segundo dados do CME Group, a maioria dos investidores espera que a instituição mantenha as taxas inalteradas. O mercado também acompanha declarações do presidente da instituição, Kevin Warsh.

🔎 A política de juros nos EUA tem reflexos no Brasil. Com as taxas em nível historicamente elevado, cresce a pressão para que a Selic, taxa básica de juros brasileira, permaneça em patamar alto por mais tempo, além de gerar efeitos sobre o câmbio.

▶️ No Brasil, o cenário fiscal segue na mira dos investidores. Na véspera, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, anunciou que o governo enviará ao Congresso um projeto de lei para estabelecer expressamente o compromisso de atingir o centro da meta fiscal em 2027.

O ministro também prometeu a proposta de regulamentação do Imposto Seletivo, conhecido como "imposto do pecado". As medidas vêm em meio à pressão de investidores e empresários por um reajuste fiscal por parte do governo, após a reeleição de Lula (PT).

▶️ No mercado de commodities, os preços do petróleo continuaram elevados , após os EUA orientarem países do Golfo a se prepararem para uma possível campanha militar contra o Irã após as eleições legislativas, em 3 de novembro. As informações são do Wall Street Journal.

Perto das 9h, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, subia 1,16%, cotado a US$ 115,20. Já o WTI , referência nos EUA, avançava 1,83%, a US$ 101,73 por barril.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Investidores e empresários intensificaram a pressão fiscal sobre o governo nesta semana, após a reeleição do presidente Lula (PT) para um quarto mandato no último domingo (25).

A preocupação é que o descontrole piore a situação da dívida pública e traga uma deterioração nas condições financeiras do país, com crédito mais caro e a possibilidade de uma nova alta da Selic caso a valorização do dólar pressione a inflação.

Com isso, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou, na véspera, que o governo federal enviará ao Congresso Nacional um projeto de lei para estabelecer expressamente o compromisso de atingir o centro da meta fiscal em 2027.

Ao mirar o centro da meta, em tese, o governo poderá precisar bloquear mais recursos ao longo de 2027, limitando os gastos dos ministérios.

"Depois da eleição, o presidente vai definir a equipe dele, depois a equipe vai apresentar quais serão essas medidas em termos de ajuste, em termos de perseguição da meta, para mostrar que o compromisso nosso, o compromisso desse governo do presidente é com responsabilidade fiscal", disse o ministro.

Sem dar detalhes, Durigan também afirmou que a equipe econômica prepara outras medidas para reforçar a confiança na trajetória das contas públicas.

"Nós vamos dizer e dar todos os instrumentos para que a gente não tenha dúvida jurídica que a gente vai perseguir o centro da meta [fiscal]. Mas existem outras medidas que estão sendo avaliadas, então agora nós temos uma etapa", declarou a jornalistas.

O ministro também afirmou que a equipe econômica se prepara para enviar ao Congresso a proposta de regulamentação do Imposto Seletivo, conhecido como "imposto do pecado". A expectativa é que o texto seja enviado ainda nesta semana.

Criado pela reforma tributária sobre o consumo, o imposto do pecado começará a ser cobrado em 2027 e tem o objetivo de encarecer produtos ou atividades que causam danos à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.

A lista inclui bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros. O novo imposto também incidirá sobre alguns veículos, conforme o nível de poluição, sobre a extração de bens minerais e sobre loterias, apostas e jogos de fantasy sports.

Na Ásia , as ações chinesas voltaram a subir nesta quarta-feira, acompanhando a recuperação dos papéis de inteligência artificial após os resultados financeiros mais otimistas da fabricante de chips SK Hynix.

O SSEC , Índice de Xangai, e o CSI300 , que reúne grandes empresas chinesas, subiram 0,9% na sessão. No Japão, o Nikkei avançou 1,08% e o Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, valorizou 6,63%. O Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, teve ganhos de 0,23%.

* Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters.

articles.title: Marabraz tem recuperação judicial aceita pela Justiça e diz que buscará 'solução sustentável' para os negócios | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão suspende cobranças judiciais por 180 dias e dá 60 dias para a rede apresentar um plano de pagamento aos credores; lojas poderão continuar funcionando durante o processo.
articles.summary: Decisão suspende cobranças judiciais por 180 dias e dá 60 dias para a rede apresentar um plano de pagamento aos credores; lojas poderão continuar funcionando durante o processo.
articles.body:
Lojas Marabraz. — Foto: Divulgação/Lojas Marabrez

A Justiça de São Paulo aceitou o pedido de recuperação judicial do Grupo Marabraz , rede de móveis que busca renegociar cerca de R$ 140 milhões em dívidas.

A decisão foi assinada na terça-feira (27) pela juíza Fernanda Perez Jacomini, da 3ª Vara de Falências e Recuperações Judiciais da capital.

"A empresa informa que cumprirá as determinações judiciais e apresentará seu plano de recuperação no prazo legal estabelecido, buscando uma solução sustentável para a continuidade dos negócios e manutenção de seu compromisso com a atransparência e o diálogo com colaboradores, clientes, fornecedores e parceiros", afirma a empresa em nota enviada ao g1 .

O processo abrange seis empresas do grupo, incluindo a Marabraz Comercial Ltda., responsável pelo registro da marca, e outras cinco companhias ligadas às operações da rede.

🔎 O objetivo da recuperação judicial é permitir que as empresas reorganizem suas finanças e negociem suas dívidas com os credores, sob supervisão da Justiça, para tentar manter as atividades e evitar a falência.

Na decisão, a juíza determinou a suspensão , por 180 dias, das execuções de dívidas sujeitas à recuperação judicial.

A medida impede temporariamente que os credores cobrem esses débitos por meio de determinadas ações judiciais e tomem bens das empresas para receber os valores, respeitadas as exceções previstas em lei.

A decisão também determina que as empresas apresentem um plano de recuperação judicial em até 60 dias.

O documento deverá detalhar como pretendem reorganizar as finanças e pagar os credores. O plano será submetido às etapas previstas na legislação, e o descumprimento do prazo pode levar à decretação da falência.

A juíza, no entanto, não autorizou, neste momento, que o patrimônio e as dívidas das seis empresas sejam tratados como se pertencessem a uma única companhia.

Embora façam parte do mesmo grupo econômico, a perícia judicial não encontrou documentação suficiente para comprovar uma mistura generalizada dos bens e das obrigações das empresas.

Com isso, o processo seguirá pelo regime de consolidação processual, no qual as empresas podem conduzir a recuperação judicial em conjunto, mas precisam manter separadas as informações financeiras e as relações com seus credores.

Cada uma deverá apresentar sua própria relação de credores e seu plano de recuperação.

A Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Consultores foi nomeada administradora judicial. A empresa ficará responsável por acompanhar as atividades e as finanças das devedoras, além de apresentar relatórios periódicos à Justiça.

A decisão também concedeu às empresas um prazo adicional, improrrogável, de 15 dias para apresentar documentos que ainda estavam pendentes, como extratos bancários específicos e certidões de protesto de filiais desativadas . Se as exigências não forem cumpridas, o processamento da recuperação judicial poderá ser revogado.

A Justiça determinou que as concessionárias Enel e CPFL não interrompam o fornecimento de energia elétrica nas unidades com contratos ativos por causa de dívidas anteriores ao pedido de recuperação judicial.

A decisão não obriga, porém, a reativação de instalações cujos contratos já haviam sido encerrados regularmente, salvo se as empresas comprovarem que o desligamento ocorreu exclusivamente por causa de débitos anteriores sujeitos à recuperação.

A juíza também autorizou que as empresas retirem mercadorias, mostruários, equipamentos e outros bens de sua propriedade de imóveis comerciais que ocupavam anteriormente.

Os locadores deverão permitir a entrada das equipes autorizadas em até dez dias após receberem uma notificação prévia com data e horário. A medida não impede o andamento de ações de despejo.

Ao anunciar o pedido de recuperação judicial, a Marabraz afirmou que a decisão foi motivada por dificuldades enfrentadas pelo varejo, conflitos na estrutura familiar que dava suporte às operações e restrições de acesso ao crédito.

articles.title: Ministério do Idoso: Lula planeja criar nova pasta no governo | G1
articles.standfirst: Auxiliares do presidente tiveram conversas com especialistas da UERJ e querem aproveitar a experiência da Universidade Aberta da Terceira Idade.
articles.summary: O presidente Lula planeja criar o Ministério do Idoso com foco em saúde e proteção social, avaliando o nome do médico Alexandre Cardoso para comandar a nova pasta.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidiu criar o Ministério do Idoso para seu quarto mandato. O blog apurou que auxiliares próximos de Lula procuraram especialistas do setor para montar um ministério que inclua atenção social, em saúde e proteção desta faixa da população.

Auxiliares de Lula querem aproveitar a experiência da Universidade Aberta da Terceira Idade, integrada ao Núcleo do Envelhecimento Humano da Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro.

Um dos nomes cotados para comandar o ministério é o do médico e ex-deputado federal Alexandre Cardoso, que foi secretário de Ciência e Tecnologia do governo do Rio de Janeiro na gestão de Sérgio Cabral e trabalha em projetos para terceira idade, entre eles o de inclusão digital e social.

No discurso de vitória de Lula, na noite de domingo (25), o presidente reeleito agradeceu o voto de idosos, muitos dos quais foram às urnas mesmo sem a obrigatoriedade de votar por terem mais de 70 anos.

Ao celebrar seus 81 anos, nesta terça-feira (27), Lula recebeu idosos e voltou a falar da importância do voto deles.

“Eu estava vendo o vídeo dos velhinhos votarem. Eu, sinceramente, acho que foi a imagem mais forte e humana que já vi em uma eleição”, disse.

A Secretaria de Comunicação da Presidência não confirma as conversas para criação de um novo ministério.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em evento no Instituto Nacional de Traumatologia e Ortopedia (Into), no Rio de Janeiro, em 17 de julho de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/Ricardo Stuckert

articles.title: TCU propõe alíquota de 11,3% para o futuro imposto sobre consumo do governo federal em 2027; Senado tem que aprovar valor | G1
articles.standfirst: Para fazer cálculo, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com impostos que serão extintos neste ano, pois reforma prevê manter carga tributária. Proposta será enviada ao Congresso. Caberá ao Senado fixar valor final do tributo até 15 de dezembro.
articles.summary: Para fazer cálculo, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com impostos que serão extintos neste ano, pois reforma prevê manter carga tributária. Proposta será enviada ao Congresso. Caberá ao Senado fixar valor final do tributo até 15 de dezembro.
articles.body:
O plenário do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) aprovou nesta quarta-feira (28) uma proposta para que a alíquota da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), novo tributo aprovado na reforma tributária sobre o consumo, seja de 11,3% em 2027.

O cálculo foi feito por técnicos do tribunal com base em dados da Receita Federal. O valor será encaminhado ao Congresso Nacional, que poderá concordar ou não. Caberá ao Senado fixar o valor final da alíquota, que será cobrada a partir de 2027. Se o Senado não aprovar uma alíquota até 15 de dezembro, terá validade o valor calculado pelo TCU.

▶️Para calcular o valor da CBS, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com os impostos que estão sendo extintos no fim de 2026 (PIS, Cofins e grande parte do IPI).

Isso porque, uma das premissas da reforma sobre o consumo, é manter o atual patamar da carga tributária.

O governo informou, na proposta de orçamento de 2027, que espera arrecadar R$ 636 bilhões com a CBS no ano que vem.

A proposta do TCU também engloba um "redutor" de 44,2% na alíquota de referência da CBS, e alíquotas reduzidas para alguns produtos e serviços, nas compras públicas.

🔎 O TCU é responsável por analisar e homologar os cálculos das alíquotas de referência da CBS e do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS), etapas previstas na transição para o novo sistema tributário brasileiro, aprovada pelo Congresso Nacional em 2023.

🔎A CBS substituirá o PIS, a Contribuição para Financiamento da Seguridade Social (Cofins) e, também, uma parte do Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI).

🔎 PIS e Cofins serão extintas em 2026, enquanto o IPI permanecerá somente para itens produzidos na Zona Franca de Manaus (ZFM) — mas com tributação efetiva somente no resto do país.

Moedas, trocado, dinheiro, troco, real — Foto: Freepik

🔎 Em 2024, o governo estimou que a alíquota da CBS seria de 8,8%. Entretanto, nos meses seguintes foram feitas novas exceções à cobrança do imposto cheio que elevaram a alíquota.

🔎 A área econômica não fez nova projeção, mas cálculo da consultoria Roit aponta para uma alíquota de 9,43% em 2027.

🔎 Estimativas divulgadas em julho pelo Comitê Gestor do IBS, dos estados, apontam que a CBS teria uma taxa de cerca de 9,2% no próximo ano.

Além da CBS do governo federal, a reforma tributária também contempla a cobrança do IBS estadual e municipal, que terá uma alíquota marginal, de 0,1% em 2027 e em 2028.

A partir de 2029, os estados e municípios começam a aumentar, gradualmente, a cobrança do IBS, até 2032. A cobrança integral começa em 2033.

Assim que a alíquota cheia estiver sendo cobrada, estimativas apontam que o imposto sobre o consumo do governo federal, estados e municípios, somará cerca de 28% em 2033 — o primeiro ano com tributação cheia — uma das maiores alíquotas do mundo.

O valor, que supera o teto existente de 26,5%, ficaria acima do registrado nos países ricos.

Esse será o nível necessário para manter a atual carga tributária sobre o consumo, ou seja, o peso dos impostos sobre essa base de tributação.

Tributos altos sobre o consumo, por sua vez, penalizam a população de baixa renda — uma vez que uma parte maior de sua renda é destinada aos impostos.

➡️O governo federal, por sua vez, alega que, atualmente, os impostos cobrados sobre o consumo no país são ainda maiores, com tributação média de cerca de 34% – há dificuldade em calcular o peso dos impostos pois o sistema é muito complexo, há exceções, e os tributos incidem sobre si mesmos. Com a reforma tributária, eles passarão a ser cobrados por fora (aparecerão separados do valor do produto ou serviço).

A aprovação de exceções à alíquota cheia dos futuros impostos sobre o consumo durante a tramitação da reforma tributária no Congresso Nacional, ou seja, de benefícios para setores e produtos, é uma das responsáveis pelo elevado nível da tributação estimada para os futuros imposto s — algo que foi apontado, à época, por exemplo, pela indústria nacional.

A explicação é que, quanto maior é o número de exceções, ou regimes diferenciados — com tratamento favorecido —, mais alta é a chamada "alíquota padrão", ou seja, que os demais setores da economia, não englobados por benefícios, têm de pagar.

Isso por conta da determinação da reforma de manter o atual patamar da carga tributária — valor que se arrecada em proporção ao PIB. Com setores e produtos beneficiados por exceções aprovadas pelo Legislativo, com tributação menor, todo os consumidores pagam a mais na alíquota normal (chamada de padrão).

Entre os benefícios aprovados na tramitação da reforma tributária, estão alíquota zero para a cesta básica, incluindo as proteínas (o que, segundo especialistas, beneficia a população mais rica), para uma lista de medicamentos e dispositivos médicos.

O Congresso aprovou ainda alíquotas reduzidas para serviços de educação e saúde; medicamentos e dispositivos médicos; produções artísticas, culturais, jornalísticas e audiovisuais nacionais; atividades desportivas; e profissões regulamentadas e fiscalizadas por conselhos profissionais.

Esses dois novos impostos que serão implementados gradualmente até 2032 funcionarão no modelo de imposto sobre valor agregado (IVA), como acontece no resto do mundo, de maneira não cumulativa.

Isso significa que, ao longo da cadeia de produção, o imposto é cobrado em cada etapa, mas os contribuintes podem descontar o tributo pago anteriormente.

Por exemplo: se o IVA for de 20%, um produto vendido ao consumidor final por R$ 100 terá imposto de R$ 20, que, ao final da cadeia, totalizará R$ 20, após os mecanismos de crédito e compensação entre as diferentes empresas da produção e comercialização.

Outra mudança é que os tributos sobre o consumo (IVA) serão cobrados no "destino", ou seja, no local onde os produtos são consumidos, e não mais onde eles são produzidos. A migração da origem para o destino será feita de forma gradual durante décadas.

Isso contribuirá para combater a chamada "guerra fiscal", nome dado a disputa entre os estados para que empresas se instalem em seus territórios. Para isso, intensificam a concessão de benefícios fiscais.

Além dos tributos não cumulativos do governo, estados e municípios, a reforma tributária prevê, ainda, a cobrança do chamado "imposto seletivo", também chamado de imposto do pecado.

Para que tenha validade, esse novo tributo ainda tem de ser regulamentado. Nesta terça-feira (27), o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou que a proposta para o imposto seletivo será enviada ao Congresso Nacional em breve, provavelmente ainda nesta semana.

O imposto do pecado começará a ser cobrado em 2027 e tem o objetivo de encarecer produtos ou atividades que causam danos à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.

A lista inclui bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros. O novo imposto também incidirá sobre alguns veículos, conforme o nível de poluição, sobre a extração de bens minerais e sobre loterias, apostas e jogos de fantasy sports.

Em junho, o Ministério da Fazenda informou que a ideia é manter, pelo menos em um primeiro momento, a carga tributária atual , sem aumento dos impostos durante a transição. Nesse período, o governo pretende discutir as mudanças com os setores afetados.

O TCU informou que essa projeção do governo federal foi considerada para manter a atual carga tributária sobre o consumo.

articles.title: INSS desmente bloqueio de benefício por falta de biometria; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Exigência vale para novos pedidos feitos desde 21 de novembro de 2025. Instituto alerta para golpes que usam mensagens falsas para obter dados pessoais.
articles.summary: Exigência vale para novos pedidos feitos desde 21 de novembro de 2025. Instituto alerta para golpes que usam mensagens falsas para obter dados pessoais.
articles.body:
O Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) esclareceu que é falsa a informação de que beneficiários precisam apresentar um documento com biometria até 20 de novembro para evitar o bloqueio de pagamentos.

Segundo o órgão, a exigência se aplica somente a novos pedidos de benefícios feitos a partir de 21 de novembro de 2025 . O instituto também reforçou que não é necessário comparecer a uma agência para realizar o cadastro biométrico.

O registro é feito quando o cidadão solicita documentos oficiais que utilizam esse tipo de identificação, como a Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN), a Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) ou o título de eleitor.

A biometria consiste no registro de características físicas, como impressões digitais e imagem do rosto, para confirmar a identidade de uma pessoa e auxiliar na concessão de benefícios previdenciários e assistenciais, como aposentadorias, auxílios e o Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC/Loas).

O cadastro biométrico para a Carteira de Identidade Nacional consiste na coleta das impressões digitais dos dedos das duas mãos e da fotografia do rosto do cidadão, que são armazenadas em uma base de dados oficial do governo federal.

O objetivo é confirmar a identidade do beneficiário e impedir que terceiros recebam valores indevidamente.

Quem solicitar benefícios ao INSS deverá comprovar registro biométrico em bases oficiais do governo, como:

Carteira de Identidade Nacional ( CIN );

Carteira Nacional de Habilitação ( CNH ).

A exigência já vinha sendo aplicada de forma parcial. Desde setembro de 2024, ela é obrigatória para pedidos do BPC/Loas. O governo também já utiliza o cadastro biométrico em outras frentes, como no empréstimo consignado de aposentados e pensionistas.

A nova portaria regulamenta e amplia essa exigência para a maior parte dos benefícios previdenciários e assistenciais requeridos ao INSS, abrangendo os pedidos apresentados a partir de novembro de 2025.

Para quem já recebe benefícios, a implementação será gradual e não haverá bloqueio automático neste momento.

Mesmo entre os novos pedidos, há situações em que a apresentação de documento com biometria é dispensada. De acordo com as regras informadas pelo INSS, estão entre as exceções:

Idade superior a 80 anos: basta Cadastro Nacional de Informações Sociais (CNIS) ou documento com foto;

Migrantes, refugiados ou apátridas: protocolos de solicitação de refúgio ou reconhecimento de apatridia, ou Carteira de Registro Nacional Migratório (CRNM) e Documento Provisório de Registro Nacional Migratório (DPRNM);

Residentes no exterior: declaração consular, Apostila de Haia ou acordo internacional de previdência;

Impossibilidade de deslocamento: atestado médico emitido nos últimos 30 dias;

Localidade de difícil acesso: documentos como Imposto de Renda, contrato de locação, contas de consumo ou Cadastro Único (CadÚnico);

Requerentes de salário-maternidade, benefício por incapacidade ou pensão por morte , conforme previsto na portaria.

Além disso, a exigência não se aplica aos pedidos de salário-maternidade, benefícios por incapacidade e pensão por morte.

O governo considera válidos registros biométricos já existentes em bases oficiais.

1. Confira seus documentos: verifique se já possui biometria em ao menos um destes:

Título de eleitor (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral);

Se você já possui biometria registrada em qualquer uma dessas bases oficiais, não é necessário realizar uma nova coleta.

2. Consulte canais oficiais: a checagem pode ser feita em serviços digitais do governo, como o gov.br , além de plataformas da Justiça Eleitoral e dos Detrans, que informam se há biometria cadastrada. Segundo o Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS), mais de 150 milhões de brasileiros já possuem biometria registrada em bases federais.

3. Se não tiver registro biométrico: pelas regras de transição do governo, quem ainda não possui nenhum cadastro biométrico deverá providenciar a partir de janeiro de 2027 a emissão da Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN), que se tornará a principal referência para identificação biométrica nos benefícios sociais.

Já para quem possui biometria cadastrada — seja na Justiça Eleitoral, na CNH ou no passaporte — a obrigatoriedade do documento passa a valer a partir de janeiro de 2028.

🔎 O primeiro passo para emitir a CIN é acessar o site gov.br/identidade , fazer o agendamento no sistema do estado e marcar a coleta da biometria. No atendimento, é necessário apresentar certidão de nascimento ou de casamento. A versão digital do documento permite incluir outros registros, como CNH e título de eleitor.

O governo também disponibilizará, até 31 de dezembro de 2026, o Serviço de Verificação Biométrica aos órgãos responsáveis pela gestão dos benefícios da seguridade social.

A ferramenta permitirá confirmar a identidade dos cidadãos por meio de dados biométricos, como impressões digitais e reconhecimento facial.

Quem já recebe benefício precisa fazer biometria?

Não imediatamente. Segundo o governo, a implementação da exigência será gradual e não haverá bloqueio automático dos benefícios em andamento.

Durante o período de transição, quem já era beneficiário de programas sociais até 31 de dezembro de 2026 continuará com o cadastro aceito.

Além disso, até 31 de dezembro de 2027, também serão válidas as biometrias registradas no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), na Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) ou no passaporte, desde que tenham sido coletadas até 31 de dezembro de 2026.

A partir de 1º de janeiro de 2028, a biometria da Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN) passará a ser o padrão para a concessão, manutenção e renovação de benefícios sociais. Quem já possui a CIN não precisará realizar um novo cadastro biométrico, pois a base do documento é única.

Já as pessoas que ainda não têm nenhum registro biométrico deverão emitir a Carteira de Identidade Nacional dentro do cronograma estabelecido pelo governo.

🔎 O que acontece se a biometria não for apresentada? Nos casos em que ela for exigida para a solicitação de um benefício, o requerente que não comprovar biometria nem demonstrar que se enquadra em uma das hipóteses de dispensa dentro do prazo poderá ter o pedido encerrado e considerado desistente. Segundo o Ministério da Previdência Social, a medida busca reforçar a identificação dos beneficiários e reduzir fraudes.

Medida vem sendo implementada de forma gradual

Prédio do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS). — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

A exigência da biometria vem sendo adotada de forma escalonada pelo governo federal. Em abril, o Executivo adiou o cronograma de expansão total, que agora prevê implantação completa apenas em janeiro de 2027 .

Até lá, a regra segue sendo ampliada por etapas. Atualmente, já vale para alguns pedidos, como aposentadorias, enquanto outras modalidades foram incluídas em fases posteriores.

O plano inicial previa uma ampliação da exigência em 2026, incluindo benefícios como auxílio por incapacidade temporária, pensão por morte, seguro-desemprego, abono salarial, Bolsa Família e salário-maternidade, mas esse cronograma foi revisto.

À época, o governo afirmou que o novo calendário buscava dar mais tempo para que a população emita a Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN) e faça o cadastro biométrico sem risco de exclusão.

O INSS esclarece que o cadastro biométrico e a prova de vida são procedimentos diferentes . Atualmente, a comprovação de vida dos beneficiários é realizada automaticamente pelo instituto, por meio do cruzamento de dados.

Caso seja necessária alguma providência por parte do cidadão, ele será comunicado pelos canais oficiais do INSS ou do governo federal.

Por isso, não é necessário comparecer a uma agência para fazer a prova de vida ou apresentar biometria apenas por causa de mensagens que circulam na internet.

Quem tiver dúvidas sobre a situação do benefício pode consultar o aplicativo ou site Meu INSS ou entrar em contato com a Central Telefônica 135.

O instituto também alerta para tentativas de fraude que utilizam informações falsas sobre biometria e bloqueio de benefícios para obter dados pessoais dos cidadãos.

Segundo o órgão, servidores não são enviados às casas dos beneficiários para realizar a comprovação de vida . O INSS também não solicita senhas, dados bancários ou transferências de dinheiro para esse procedimento.

A orientação é não clicar em links desconhecidos nem fornecer informações pessoais em páginas suspeitas. Criminosos podem utilizar sites falsos para capturar dados e aplicá-los em outras fraudes.

Em caso de dúvida, o cidadão deve consultar os canais oficiais do instituto, como o Meu INSS, a Central Telefônica 135 e o p ortal gov.br/inss .

articles.title: Focus on covering more people, not just higher premiums: Irdai
articles.summary: Mumbai: Insurance companies must focus on covering more people and delivering effective protection for every rupee spent, rather than seeking higher
articles.body: Mumbai: Insurance companies must focus on covering more people and delivering effective protection for every rupee spent, rather than seeking higher premiums from existing policyholders, Irdai chairman Ajay Seth said.He also called for online insurance platforms to stick to their core role of helping customers compare products and buy policies, rather than expanding into physical distribution, using dynamic pricing or demanding contact details and do-not-disturb waiver before providing quotes.“We have to change our lens,” Seth said. “Instead of measuring insurance penetration and density, the industry should track lives and businesses covered, the effectiveness of protection and cover per rupee spent.” He was speaking during a fireside chat at a Business Standard BFSI event.Insurers serve the top 10-15% of the population reasonably well, but extending meaningful cover to the top 50% requires better affordability and quality. “Instead of chasing existing people for higher cover we should go for covering more people,” he said, adding that insurance must grow faster than the economy, not slower.Seth said digital insurance platforms should offer simplified products for easy price comparison and help customers find suitable cover at the lowest price. They should not dilute this role by building physical distribution networks, which operate on different dynamics. He also cautioned against the practice of offering dynamic pricing for covers by online platforms.“Dynamic pricing works in the airline industry, not in insurance,” he said, ruling out price changes on digital platforms. Customers should be able to compare prices without sharing personal details. Regulatory guardrails are needed to keep platforms focused on their core purpose.Health insurance is growing general insurance at 1.3 times the economy’s pace, but high customer dissatisfaction threatens to undermine growth. Seth called this an “uneasy, unstable equilibrium” and said insurers must disclose how much of the premiums they collect, they actually pay out in health insurance claims.Current settlement rates do not show this. “That information neither we track nor is it in the public domain,” he said. Seth was critical of the high churn in the health insurance portfolio under the guise of portability to show increased new business.Irdai is consulting insurers, intermediaries and policyholder representatives on distribution reforms to cut acquisition costs and ease premium pressure. Health insurance commissions average 24% across new policies and renewals; reducing them to 15-20% is the objective, he said. The regulator also wants to cut health insurance paperwork through the National Health Exchange. articles.title: Das flags priorities for banks to sustain growth
articles.summary: Mumbai: India’s 8% growth target is within reach, but sustaining that pace will require banks and financial institutions to finance infrastructure,
articles.body: Mumbai: India’s 8% growth target is within reach, but sustaining that pace will require banks and financial institutions to finance infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and smaller businesses while expanding insurance and pension coverage, former RBI governor Shaktikanta Das said on Tuesday.He called for deeper credit and bond markets and a shift in household savings from physical assets to productive financial investments to support India’s ambition of becoming a developed economy by 2047.“In fact, in the recent months, I have stated on record that India is in a striking distance of 8% growth,” Das said in his keynote address at the Business Standard BFSI Summit 2026 here. He attributed the momentum to “the triple engines of macroeconomic stability; continuing structural reforms; and strategic policy initiatives to develop domestic capacity where we are largely import dependent”.Sustaining growth would be harder amid geopolitical conflicts, trade barriers, sanctions, unilateral tariffs and supply chain disruptions. Unlike earlier shocks, these disruptions had become prolonged, threatening energy and commodity markets, economic activity and financial stability. Das cautioned that consumption-related household borrowing required “careful and consistent monitoring”, signalling the need for continued scrutiny even as aggregate indicators improved.He identified stronger bank balance sheets as a key improvement, with lenders moving beyond high bad loans and weak capital adequacy to become well-capitalised and profitable.You use AI every day. articles.title: India-Mexico PTA: Talks aim to deepen trade and investment ties
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India and Mexico have begun negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA), as both countries signing the Terms of Reference to set the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and Mexico have begun negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA), as both countries signing the Terms of Reference to set the scope and roadmap for discussions. The proposed agreement aims to expand bilateral trade, encourage investment, create business opportunities and develop a more diversified supply chain.The negotiations follow an agreement between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to deepen the bilateral partnership during the G-7 Summit in Canada in June 2025.The Terms of Reference establish the framework, scope and modalities for the negotiations. The discussions will cover market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, dispute settlement, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade and trade remedies.The proposed PTA is intended to be mutually beneficial and balanced, with the aim of creating new economic opportunities for both countries.Automotive, pharmaceuticals and electronics among potential sectorsThe agreement seeks to build on the complementary strengths of the Indian and Mexican economies and expand opportunities for Mexican products and businesses in the Indian market.Mexico is an important market for Indian exporters and investors and has strong links to global value chains. The sectors identified as having broad potential for cooperation include automotive, chemicals, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agri-food, energy, critical minerals, medical devices and advanced manufacturing.Commerce secretary leads discussions with Mexican delegationDuring commerce secretary Rajesh Aggarwal's visit, the Indian and Mexican delegations discussed bilateral relations and ways to increase trade and investment flows.Mexico's deputy minister of foreign trade, Luis Rosendo Gutierrez Romano, participated in the discussions on behalf of Minister of Economic Affairs Marcelo Ebrard Casaubon.The two sides also reviewed the broader bilateral economic agenda, identifying opportunities to strengthen cooperation, deepen trade and investment ties, and build stronger connections between the productive sectors of both countries.India and Mexico also discussed the possibility of a Mexican business delegation visiting India during the first quarter of 2027.The proposed mission is intended to facilitate business-to-business (B2B) meetings, help identify business opportunities and strengthen trade ties between the productive sectors of the two countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: NPA generation bottomed out in FY26: ICRA
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Banks' fresh non-performing asset (NPA) generation is expected to rise moderately in FY27 as asset quality normalises after a prolonged
articles.body: MUMBAI: Banks' fresh non-performing asset (NPA) generation is expected to rise moderately in FY27 as asset quality normalises after a prolonged improvement, while credit growth and profitability remain firm, according to ICRA.Public sector banks' fresh slippages, which fell from Rs 1.8 lakh crore in FY22 to Rs 90,000 crore in FY25 and FY26, are projected to rise to Rs 1 lakh crore in FY27. The gross fresh NPA generation rate is estimated at around 0.8% in FY27, unchanged from FY26.Private sector banks are expected to see fresh slippages rise to Rs 1.3 lakh crore in FY27 from Rs 1.2 lakh crore in FY26. Their annualised fresh NPA generation rate is projected to remain in the 1.6-1.8% range, reflecting their greater exposure to unsecured retail and MSME loans.Despite the expected increase in fresh slippages, overall asset quality is projected to remain stable. Gross NPAs are estimated at 1.7-1.8% of advances and net NPAs at 0.4-0.5% by March 2027.Bank profitability is expected to remain steady, with return on assets projected at 1.27-1.34% in FY27. Credit growth, margin expansion and contained credit costs are expected to support earnings.Bank credit is projected to grow by 15.1-15.9% in FY27, translating into incremental lending of Rs 32.3 lakh crore to Rs 33.8 lakh crore. Retail and MSME lending are expected to support growth, alongside a pickup in corporate credit. Elevated bond yields are making bank loans more attractive to companies than bond market borrowing.Interest rate movements and funding costs will also influence margins. Banks' large share of variable-rate loans allows lending rates to adjust as the interest rate cycle turns, supporting yields on advances.Foreign currency non-resident (FCNR(B)) deposit inflows, supported by the RBI's concessional swap facility, have added liquidity to the banking system. This is expected to support credit expansion and help contain funding costs by reducing banks' reliance on more expensive wholesale deposits.Floating-rate housing loans and other longer-tenure products will also transmit benchmark rate changes to borrowers, helping banks sustain spreads.Credit costs are expected to remain below levels seen during earlier periods of stress. Provisions for public and private sector banks are projected at around 0.4% of advances in FY27, limiting the impact of higher fresh slippages on profits.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Ideas are scarce, it’s capital that is in abundance’
articles.summary: If you have a business idea that you believe in, there is no dearth of capital, said Asish Mohapatra, co-founder of two unicorns, OfBusiness and Oxyzo.
articles.body: If you have a business idea that you believe in, there is no dearth of capital, said Asish Mohapatra, co-founder of two unicorns, OfBusiness and Oxyzo. But then came the caveat: “If you look for equity first, you will miss the bus. You have to believe that the scarcity is on your (ideas) side and the abundance is on the capital side.”Instead, extract cash straight from the operations, through cus - tomer advances or supplier credit. Failing that, tap into debt, where India’s liquidity runs a massive 20 to 22 times the availability of equity.At the TOI Ideas for India 2026 summit, industry heavyweights dissected the evolving economy and the new opportunities, including the future of AI, global capability centres (GCCs) and startups.“It’s like Rancho said in ‘3 Idiots’. If you chase excellence, everything else chases you. In the beginning, they (investors) all invest behind the person,” said Mohapatra. Across the aisle, Optum Global senior V-P Surinder Singh shifted the lens to the grass - roots — the medium- and small-scale indus - tries that form the bulk of the Indian econo - my.Given a chance to invest, Singh wouldn’t place his money into a mega-factory. He would invest it on shared digital capabilities for lakhs of starved MSMEs. While behemoths easily absorb advanced tech, small businesses are left stranded without demand forecasting or logistics intelligence.“Productivity cannot stop with large companies,” Singh said. Responding to a similar opportunity to in - vest, Mohapatra bypassed tech glamour entire - ly, arguing that India’s core structural foundations remain cracked and needs capital.“India lacks the ability to build the tools that can create the future,” he said, urging capital injection into heavy manufacturing, traditional thermalbacked power, infrastructure, and logistics.While green energy grabs headlines, “making thermal power efficient is what I would rather put money into”, said Mohapatra. On the question of AI, both speakers had compelling arguments to make.While Mohapatra stands as a watchful sceptic, maintaining that the immediate cost of AI implementation far outweighs returns for any business. Singh counters that AI isn’t an innovation theory anymore, it’s the core operating agenda.The bottleneck isn’t buying the software, it’s building the data governance and risk frameworks to survive the future. “The prob lem for organisations that don’t see benefits, or that are holding back and watching from a distance, is organisational readiness,” said Singh.In the end, Mohapatra revealed that his founders’ fund has backed 50 to 60 startups in manufacturing and financial services, proving that a new wave of unicorn founders is recycling wealth back into smaller players.And on the GCC front, with legacy IT hiring hitting a wall, India’s 2,500 GCCs, which have mutated from cheap back-offices into global innovation powerhouses, Singh delivered the final verdict. “We are very far from peak GCC.”You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Need more help. Indian innovation runs on charity’
articles.summary: I’ve spent at least a year talking to a lot of innovators around the country, and I can probably say innovation in India runs on charity,” actor Avinash
articles.body: I’ve spent at least a year talking to a lot of innovators around the country, and I can probably say innovation in India runs on charity,” actor Avinash Tiwary said at TOI Ideas for India 2026.On his visits to Hyderabad and Bengaluru, he had met innovators, including engineering students developing solutions for agriculture and mining. Their ideas were often strong, he said; however, the harder part was getting access to laboratories, grants and funding to build prototypes.Drawing on India’s emergence as an IT powerhouse, Tiwary called for more support for homegrown innovation. Citing Telangana’s T-Works, he urged people to build more prototyping facilities for building and testing new products.He also called for a clearer understanding of entrepreneurship, distinguishing between creating value in an existing market and creating an entirely new one. That need to build Indian capabilities felt especially urgent when he spoke about AI.Dependence on overseas large language models (LLMs), he warned, could leave users vulnerable if access were restricted. “When we sit and talk about closed borders, a foreign country can just switch off its LLMs, and we won’t be able to talk about agents anymore.”Tiwary also wondered whether young Indians were chasing too narrow a range of opportunities. Acknowledging the growing influence of content creators, he cited figures he had recently read about the creator economy and India’s ambitions.“But my question is this. If a country is making trillions, and needs trillions by 2030, how does it feel when 40 per cent of that country’s youth want a slice of that 400-billion-dollar pie?” Still, he saw potential in the audiences creators have built.Their reach, he said, could help Indian products and ideas find a market as the country develops new capabilities. The question of what India could build also shaped his hopes for cinema.Filmmakers, he felt, should draw on the country’s past while imagining its future — and tell stories that could influence aspirations beyond the screen.“As an artist, that is my one desire. To see films made about the future. Indian stories that create a global impact,” he said. He believed wider global distribution could boost India’s cultural influence and talent.He felt OTT had opened doors for niche audiences and different genres, but shrinking budgets and pressure to turn a profit were encouraging safer choices.The difference between streaming and cinema, he said, would still come down to the experience. Watching at home is intimate and often solitary; theatres offer scale, sound and the pleasure of watching together. His assessment came with a touch of humour: “Even my face looks beautiful there.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Fed keeps interest rates unchanged, but two officials dissented in favor of a rate hike
articles.summary: The US central bank was widely expected to hold rates steady after increasing borrowing costs last month for the first time since 2023.
articles.body:
A pause after last month’s hike: The Federal Reserve said Wednesday it is keeping its benchmark interest rate at current levels this month after raising rates in September for the first time since 2023.

Still-stubborn inflation: The war with Iran continues to push up energy prices, with higher costs starting to spread to other goods and services. That has complicated the picture for Fed officials as they balance the impact of persistently higher inflation with higher borrowing costs on already-stretched consumers.

Two dissents: Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both opted for a quarter-point rate hike at this month’s meeting. Hammack also dissented in July, again favoring a hike. Cook has never dissented in her four years in this post.

Changes at the Fed: Chairman Kevin Warsh announced a key change in the way the central bank decides on monetary policy, reducing the number of rate-setting meetings from eight to seven next year and six the following.

Our live coverage of the Federal Reserve’s latest policy decision has ended. For more analysis, read here .

Investors responded Wednesday to Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s announcement about a major change to the Fed’s rate decision schedule.

Instead of eight rate decisions per year, the Fed will have seven next year and six the year after, Warsh said. The other meetings will be used as strategy meetings but will not include rate decisions.

The change will take place next fall, Warsh said. He described the reason for the change as creating more time and space for “strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons.”

In general, the Fed is also able to call an emergency rate-decision meeting as needed.

Investors are still adapting to Warsh’s vision for the Fed, and the announcement stood out as an important development in an otherwise as-expected Fed rate decision day.

While Wall Street is awaiting more information on the development, investors, economists and analysts are digesting what they can understand. Here’s what they’re saying:

“The Fed’s new meeting schedule appears consistent with Chairman Warsh’s push for less forward guidance and less frequent signaling to markets.” — Tony Miano, global investment strategy analyst at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “Less Fed communication could mean more market volatility.”

“Warsh reforms to enter a new phase next year.” — Thomas Ryan, senior North America economist at Capital Economics. “ We do not think this will significantly undermine the Fed’s ability to respond to incoming data, as it will still be able to assess two payrolls and CPI reports between meetings.”

“The market has adjusted to Warsh’s communication style, but there might be a ways to go before they are fully on the same page.” — Thomas Simons, chief US economist at Jefferies.

“ I think that goes along with his idea that they want to take their time and be a little bit more deliberate with policy.” — Thomas Urano, co-chief investment officer at Sage Advisory. “Maybe the thinking is that eight policy adjustments per year is just a bit too much, given the slow-moving nature of policy and its impact on the economy.”

In 2022, then-Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell was blasted for repeatedly calling inflation “transitory” as it began inching closer to 40-year highs. Powell, at the time, said he believed the pace of price increases would slow once supply chain bottlenecks cleared and more businesses could safely reopen.

But once it became clear that it was not going to fade on its own, the Fed quickly had to play catch-up to get inflation under control. Powell retired the word, but not before it became a defining part of his legacy.

Now, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is trying to convince Americans that the inflation they’re experiencing is, in fact, transitory.

“I think they should have an open mind in terms of the transitory nature of the supply shock,” Bessent said of Fed officials, in a CNBC interview on Wednesday shortly after the Fed announced its decision to leave rates unchanged at its October policy meeting.

In essence, Bessent is saying Fed officials should look past the current run-up in inflation because it predominantly stems from a rise in energy costs, which could prove temporary.

At the same time, inflation has seeped its way into a variety of goods and services beyond the pump.

The stock market gained slightly after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady Wednesday, matching Wall Street’s expectations.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite each gained almost 0.3%. The Dow rose almost 100 points, or 0.2%. The indexes are up three days in a row.

The Fed updated its policy statement to say economic activity is growing at a “strong” pace, compared to a “solid” pace in the statement in September.

During remarks, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh repeatedly asserted that the central bank is committed to reining in inflation. “We will deliver price stability, no ifs, ands or buts, and that continues to be the case,” he said.

Stocks bounced around during trading: The S&P 500 rose as much as 0.46%, gave up those gains and then pushed higher to end the day in the green.

It was the first time the S&P 500 closed higher on a Fed rate decision day since December 2025. The Fed held rates steady five meetings in a row from January to July, then raised rates in September before holding steady today.

Heading into the rate decision, traders widely expected the Fed to hold rates steady, followed by a rate hike in December. The Fed matched the market’s expectation today, and the odds for a December hike rose to 85% from 78% one day ago, according to CME FedWatch.

“This Fed still has a job to do if the type of price stability that Chair Warsh has described is to be achieved,” strategists at ING wrote in a note.

The 10-year yield rose three basis points to 5.02%. The US dollar index fell 0.2%. Gold futures dipped as much as 0.9% during trading before erasing losses and gaining 0.3%.

Two primary sources of US consumer debt – credit cards and auto loans – have been a sore point in family budgets of late.

And there is nothing to suggest much will change in the fourth quarter.

Credit cards: It doesn’t matter that the Fed left its key rate unchanged – or whether the Fed hikes or lowers rate by a quarter point or a half point in December. You are still paying a punitive rate if you carry a credit card balance.

“The average credit card rate sits around 20%,” said Bankrate credit card expert Ana Staples in an email.

You can always call your card issuers to see if they will lower your rate by a few points. But you’ll likely need a much bigger reduction to make paying off your debt feasible.

“A 0% intro APR balance transfer card is the most direct way to cut interest costs for consumers who can qualify,” Staples said.

Auto loans: The average APR on new car loans was 7% in the third quarter, according to Edmunds.com . But that masks two trends raising purchasers’ costs.

A record 25.5% of new-car buyers now finance their vehicles for 84 months or longer, and 29% of new-car buyers trading in an old car have been rolling negative equity into their new loans, said Joseph Yoon, a senior analyst at Edmunds.

So even though the Fed stood pat, such borrowers will still be charged higher-than-average rates in the fourth quarter.

One group of buyers, though, may catch a break. “Well-qualified, prime buyers with clean trades will benefit from competitive, holiday-incentivized deals, while underwater shoppers will find themselves locked into 8%-or-higher APRs just to finance vehicles they owe far more on than they are worth,” Yoon said.

Whichever group you’re in, three ways to minimize expenses: Improve your credit score. Choose the least expensive car that meets your needs. And shop for the best rate.

While the Federal Reserve did not raise interest rates on Wednesday, it is still expected to do so in December.

So, position your savings now to get the best interest rates for the foreseeable future that either beat or at least keep pace with inflation .

Online high-yield savings accounts: Thanks to the quarter-point Fed rate hike in September, many FDIC-insured online banks have increased their variable rates. The highest-paying ones are now offering between 4.3% and 4.5%, according to Bankrate.com and DepositQuest.com .

Money market funds: These offer another easy way to ensure your money is continually earning a competitive variable yield. While not FDIC-insured, they are low-risk because they invest in very short-term, high-quality government and corporate debt.

The average 7-day yield on money market funds as was 3.73% as of Tuesday, according to Crane Data. Among the largest and lowest cost money market funds is the Vanguard Federal Money Market Index, which had a 7-day yield of 3.87% on Tuesday.

Certificates of deposit: If you shop for an FDIC-insured CD through an online brokerage you’ll have your pick of bank CDs of various durations. For instance, for CDs with durations ranging from three months to five years, average rates were between 4.26% and 5.25% on Schwab.com on Wednesday morning.

But looking ahead, “CD rates may start to fall if the recent decline in Treasury yields continues,” said Ken Tumin, cofounder of Deposits.com.

US Treasuries: US bills and notes of varying durations offer a place to park your cash while earning interest and guaranteeing you will get your principal back if you hold the Treasury to maturity.

Yields on Treasuries ranging in length from three months to five years were between 4.19% and 4.89% Wednesday morning on Schwab.com .

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate breached 7% for the first time since January 2025 at the end of September, eventually climbing to a three-year high of 7.4% this month.

Last week, the average 30-year fixed mortgage eased slightly to 7.32%, according to Freddie Mac.

Home borrowing rates aren’t directly tied to the Federal Reserve’s rate decisions. Instead, they tend to track the 10-year Treasury yield, which reflects investors’ inflation expectations and outlook for future Fed policy. The 10-year Treasury yield and the broader bond market have been on a volatile ride, caught between renewed inflation fears, an oil shock tied to the Iran conflict, ballooning US deficits, and an AI investment boom.

“Even with the Fed choosing to keep rates unchanged, mortgage rates can and will likely continue to fluctuate because they reflect bond market activity and inflation data,” said Jeffrey Ruben, the president of WSFS Home Lending at WSFS Bank.

CNN experts discussed the Fed decision and Lisa Cook ahead of the midterms. Read their conversation here.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh denied any role politics played in the central bank’s decision to leave rates unchanged six days before the midterm elections.

Over the two days that Fed officials met this week to debate monetary policy, Warsh said he “didn’t hear an utterance about politics.”

“I don’t believe it had any role in the decision, not just for me, but for my colleagues around the room,” he said at the post-meeting press conference on Wednesday.

That said, he subtly hinted that the central bankers may be learning toward a hike when they meet again after the elections in December.

“It’s an information-rich interval in the coming period, having nothing to do with politics,” Warsh told reporters.

The Fed has over the past decade made several rate changes around midterm and presidential elections. Like Warsh, other Fed officials have stressed that rate decisions are made irrespective of politics.

In his post-meeting press conference Wednesday, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announced sweeping changes for the central bank in the coming years.

Instead of meeting eight times a year to vote on where interest rates should be, Warsh said officials would consider rate changes at seven of eight meetings next year and six of eight meetings in 2028.

The meetings where interest rate votes aren’t held will instead focus on “thinking anew about big questions” and longer-term issues, Warsh told reporters.

Officials’ decision to leave interest rates unchanged at this month’s meeting may end up creating more urgency to hike rates when officials reconvene again in December.

Inflation data was already running hot ahead of this month’s meeting, with price increases hitting consumers well beyond the gas pump. If that trend persists, officials may feel pressure to deliver a hike larger than September’s quarter-point move, making up for this month’s inaction and heading off further inflation.

Stocks were little changed after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady.

The S&P 500 fluctuated and was up 0.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite was down 0.1%.

In the bond market, the 10-year Treasury yield ticked higher to 5.05%.

Elsewhere, the US dollar index ticked higher. Gold futures fell 0.7%.

“While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient,” the Fed said in a statement. “Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.”

Traders’ focus now turns to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s post-meeting remarks.

“The more meaningful market risk remains Warsh’s press conference,” Ian Lyngen, head of US rates strategy at BMO Capital Markets, said in a note. “Investors will be looking for any further context for the pause.”

Federal Reserve Gov. Lisa Cook, whom Trump has repeatedly tried to oust over unproven allegations of mortgage fraud, cast a dissenting vote favoring a quarter-point interest rate hike at this month’s monetary policy meeting. The majority of officials voted to leave rates unchanged.

Trump has been vocal about his desires for the Fed to lower rates and has taken extraordinary measures, including suing former Fed Chair Jerome Powell, in an effort to bring rates down. He also recently formed a committee of his own appointees to investigate the allegations against Cook.

Cook’s lawyers have taken issue with the committee and said she would not be able to attend the hearing due to scheduling conflicts.

Cook’s dissenting vote on Wednesday was her first. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who has more frequently cast dissenting votes, also preferred a quarter-point hike.

This marks the second monetary policy meeting during Kevin Warsh’s chairmanship, which began in May, where officials on the Fed’s 12-person rate-setting committee cast dissenting votes.

Unlike the Federal Reserve’s last decision, this one was not unanimous. Two leaders — Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack – voted against today’s move. They preferred to go ahead and raise rates by a quarter point.

Cook has never dissented on a monetary policy decision; Hammack has raised concerns about inflation for months.

This month, President Donald Trump renewed his push to oust Cook from the Fed board.

Policymakers are contending with inflation that has for years stayed higher than normal. Price increases are now being driven by gas and energy costs, which have been on an upward climb since the start of the war with Iran. The job market is stable, albeit lackluster, which could make the Fed more comfortable raising rates further and slowing the economy.

In fact, Fed leaders on Wednesday said economic activity is growing at a “strong pace” and that domestic spending has been “resilient.” Job gains are keeping pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate hasn’t changed much.

The Federal Reserve on Wednesday held interest rates steady, even as inflation continues to weigh on American households.

The widely expected move leaves the Fed’s benchmark interest rate at a range between 3.75% and 4%.

In a statement, Fed leaders said uncertainty was still high, in part because of “geopolitical developments.”

Officials also said “the accumulation of more information will help” them determine next steps “to ensure a timely return of inflation” to normal levels. That new language indicates policymakers are still open to another hike down the road.

At the Fed’s September meeting, central bankers signaled another hike before the end of the year. That suggests another quarter-point increase could come when officials convene again in early December, depending on how the economy evolves.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is set to take questions at a news conference at 2:30 pm ET.

With less than a week to go until the midterm elections, he could face questions about political pressure on the central bank. While Fed leaders routinely say they operate independently and are guided by economic data, Trump has repeatedly attacked the Fed for not doing enough to stimulate the economy.

President Donald Trump has not been shy about his desire for the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates.

He specifically said he was tapping Kevin Warsh to lead the central bank because he believed Warsh would listen to him more, unlike former Chair Jerome Powell, whose term ended in May and who repeatedly resisted his calls for lower rates. But Warsh hasn’t given in to Trump, either.

His first major move as head of the central bank was last month’s rate hike, which many took as proof that he wasn’t going to let politics interfere with his job.

Trump has stood by Warsh, though. Ahead of the September meeting, Trump told reporters he spoke with Warsh and said, “You might as well vote with the board because it’s not going to matter,” referring to the Fed’s 12-person rate-setting committee Warsh sits on. Trump called that board “very hostile” and “very political,” though the Fed firmly defends its independence from political pressure.

The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates steady on Wednesday, even as officials weigh another hike this year to tame rising inflation.

Central bankers have struggled to tame inflation for years. But gas and energy prices have been on an upward climb since the war in Iran began, and came in hotter than expected in September.

Still, the Fed’s moves may only do so much. Tweaking interest rates can’t bring down gas prices, for example. Rates are designed to slow or stimulate the economy broadly and without targeting individual industries.

At his 2:30 p.m. press conference, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is likely to face questions on the Fed’s next move. His answers may be brief: Warsh has come out strong against any “forward guidance,” which was used for years to tee up future decisions.

Warsh may also face questions as to whether the Fed held off on a hike because of political pressure just days before the midterm elections.

Fed leaders defend their independence. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump has repeatedly attacked the central bank for not lowering rates, and his approval rating has tanked over cost-of-living issues.

Traders widely expect the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady today.

The CNN Business team covers each Fed rate decision. The links below direct to past coverage on Fed decision days this year.

The latest batch of inflation data showed that prices not only are climbing faster than they have in several months but also much more broadly.

The September Consumer Price Index showed that prices rose 0.6% in September, bringing the annual rate of inflation to 3.7% (that’s up from 0.4% and 3.4%, respectively, in August). About half of that monthly gain can be attributed to rising gas prices, which have shot higher because of the monthslong war in Iran.

But even when stripping out gas and food (categories that can be more volatile than others), prices were still rising faster than anticipated.

Core CPI, a closely watched gauge of underlying inflation, increased at a hotter-than-expected 0.3% monthly rate and 2.6% annual rate.

It’s not just gas. It’s the car repair, the doctor’s visit, the plane ticket, the computer upgrade, the new clothes that are experiencing uncomfortably high price hikes.

Thursday’s Personal Consumption Expenditures price index (the inflation gauge used by the Federal Reserve for its 2% target) is expected to show a similar trend: Economists expect prices to rise 0.5% from August and for the annual rate to move higher to 3.6% from 3.4%.

And it’s likely not over: A separate report on wholesale inflation showed that US businesses in September experienced their worst inflation in four years .

Stocks were little changed ahead of the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates: The S&P 500 was up 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite was flat.

Wall Street widely expects the Fed to hold interest rates steady. Economists at Bank of America are an outlier, forecasting a rate hike but acknowledging it is unlikely. Traders are pricing in a 93% chance of a hold, according to CME FedWatch.

Here’s what analysts and economists are saying ahead of the rate decision.

“ If the Fed holds … as expected, Chair Warsh will have to explain why.” —Michael Feroli, chief US economist at JPMorgan. “ A decision to leave rates unchanged less than a week before the midterm elections that goes unexplained would only encourage thoughts that policy is being driven by considerations other than employment and inflation.”

“Though the Fed is widely expected to remain on hold at this meeting, focus will be on any hawkish dissents and press conference signals on the path of rates for December and 2027.” — Mandy Xu, head of derivatives market intelligence at Cboe Global Markets.

“We expect the Chairman to avoid signaling any sort of forward guidance, but he will certainly be pressed on the recent inflation figures that came in unexpectedly hot.” — George Goncalves, head of US macro strategy at MUFG.

“A clear dichotomy has emerged: inflation data suggest more urgency, while key FOMC members continue to favor patience.” — Michael Gapen, chief US economist at Morgan Stanley. “Oil price persistence is critical: persistent shocks tend to push core inflation more than transitory ones.”

articles.title: Meesho’s Q2 loss narrows 68% as revenue grows 34%
articles.summary: Meesho Q2 net loss narrows 68% to Rs 132.4 crore as revenue rises 34%; orders, NMV and users grow, margin improves, and cash balance hits Rs 7,048 crore.
articles.body: BENGALURU: E-commerce company Meesho’s net loss narrowed 68% to Rs 132.4 crore in the September quarter from Rs 411.4 crore a year earlier, as revenue grew faster than expenses.Total income rose 31% to Rs 4,259 crore from Rs 3,254.9 crore. Revenue from operations increased 34% to Rs 4,131.6 crore.The loss was nearly unchanged from Rs 132.8 crore in the June quarter. Total expenses rose 24% year on year to Rs 4,382.3 crore. The year-earlier quarter included exceptional expenses of Rs 45 crore, while tax expenses fell to Rs 9.2 crore from Rs 80.9 crore.Orders increased 17% to 819 million. Net merchandise value (NMV), which measures the value of successfully delivered orders after returns and discounts, grew 23% to Rs 12,911 crore. Annual transacting users rose 21% to 284 million.Meesho said the timing of its flagship Mega Blockbuster Sale affected the quarterly comparison. The sale fell in the September quarter last year but moved to the December quarter this year. Comparing the 90 days before Dussehra in each year, NMV grew 33%, it said.Marketplace contribution margin, which measures revenue remaining after costs directly linked to orders, rose to 6% of NMV from 3.3% a year earlier and 4.6% in the preceding quarter. Meesho attributed the improvement to higher advertising revenue and logistics efficiencies that lowered shipment costs.The company said it would reinvest part of these gains in the user and seller experience, Meesho Mall and content commerce, and expected the margin to moderate in the near term.Advertising and sales promotion spending rose to 2.9% of NMV from 2.1% in the June quarter. Server costs increased to 2.3% from 1.9%, reflecting GPU capacity reserved ahead of the festive sale for AI workloads. Growth spending will remain elevated through the sale and the weeks around Diwali, while technology costs will stay higher until planned efficiencies take effect, it said.Quarterly free cash flow was positive at Rs 345 crore, helped by seasonal collections from customers ahead of payments to sellers. However, free cash flow over the preceding 12 months remained negative at Rs 565 crore. The company reported a cash balance of Rs 7,048 crore.Separately, Meesho appointed former Godrej Consumer Products managing director and CEO Sudhir Sitapati as an independent director for five years, subject to shareholder approval.You use AI every day.
